objective: Establish how HolyAgent can ship an @opentui/solid 0.8.x setup TUI given how its CLI is built and run, so the TUI works from both the Claude plugin and the Pi package on macOS, Linux and Windows.
scope: HolyAgent repo (read-only): /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-t3branch. How the CLI is built and shipped: packages/integrations/claude/src/generate.ts and packages/integrations/pi/src/generate.ts (bundling packages/runtime into dist/scripts/holyagent.js), the wrapper dist/scripts/holyagent and bun-flags.ts, the Claude plugin layout (is there any node_modules at runtime?), packages/integrations/pi/package.json (dependencies installed by pi install npm:...), packages/runtime/src/cli/setup.ts (the setup command and its flags), bunfig.toml and mise.toml.

OpenTUI (github.com/sst/opentui or its current home; npm @opentui/core and @opentui/solid at the newest 0.8.x): how @opentui/core loads its native renderer (bun:ffi dlopen of a per-platform package such as @opentui/core-darwin-arm64, embedded asset, or WASM), whether Bun.build can bundle it into one JS file and with what (an asset, a plugin, external), the Solid JSX transform it needs (bun plugin, babel preset, tsconfig jsxImportSource) and whether that works in a bun build bundle, its headless test renderer API, and its Bun version requirement.

Answer: which shipping options work (A: bundle everything into holyagent.js with the native library as an embedded file; B: keep OpenTUI external and resolve it from an installed package such as the Pi package node_modules, with a plain line-based fallback when it is absent; C: install it on first use with bun add into a cache; any other), with the evidence for each and the trade-offs for size, offline use, Windows and the dependency updater (mise run deps:update moves package.json caret ranges and bun.lock).
constraints: Read-only. Separate sourced facts from inference.
Report in under 600 words; put long excerpts in a file in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad and give its path.

criteria.text: The report states how @opentui/core loads its native code and whether it can be bundled by Bun.build, with sources
The report states how HolyAgent builds and runs its CLI from the plugin and the Pi package, with path:line, and which shipping options work
